newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska twins recovering from icy ordeal.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska twins recovering from icy ordeal.

text.p: Three-year-old twin sisters who wandered out alone to play in the snow and almost froze to death were battling back to health on Monday but doctors said they still had a long way to go.
The two girls, who were found by police lying huddled together in deep snow without shoes or coats in freezing temperatures on Friday morning, were still being treated for severe frostbite on Monday.
Jennifer and Kourtney Woracek, whose tiny footprints led police to where they lay, were improving, but hospital official George Reynolds said Jennifer had been "as close to dead as she could get."
Doctors upgraded her condition to fair from serious on Monday after removing her from an artificial breathing machine. She was still suffering from internal injuries and excessive frostbite.
Her heart and lungs had stopped working when she arrived at the hospital and doctors used a heart-lung bypass machine to warm her blood and get it circulating again.

Kourtney remained in stable condition. She was awake and alert but doctors were treating her for extreme frostbite to her feet, a hospital spokeswoman said. "Things are looking good but we have a long way to go. The doctors continue to be pleased with what they are seeing," she said.

Police, who bundled the girls into a squad car to rush them to the hospital, estimated they had been outside for at least 45 minutes. The girls' father called the 911 emergency number after waking up to discover them missing and the front door open.
